title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) to measure whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification), we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents with gpt-5-mini and a canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes (72 pairs) and 72 model calls. All baseline executions produced no emulator-observed faults (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics this degenerate confirmatory outcome is expected when identical generated candidates produce no baseline execution faults. We present full preregistration rationale, deterministic execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, exact inferential outputs, and concrete methodological recommendations for experiments that can meaningfully measure verifier utility under realistic baseline-error regimes.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate high-level operator intents into device-level configurations for network operations (NetOps). This intent→configuration translation can accelerate change pipelines but also risks silently violating reachability, policy, or ordering invariants and causing outages if generated text is executed without further checks. A common mitigation in deployment proposals is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture that pairs stochastic LLM generation with deterministic verification and, where needed, repair or human review. Prior work shows promising intent→configuration accuracy in constrained vendor dialects [1] and prototype co-pilots that include verification components [2], yet systematic, preregistered experiments that measure verifier detection performance against executed outcomes remain scarce [3].

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment that isolates verifier detection on identical LLM outputs under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The central research question is: does inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM generator and emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of configurations that execute with operational faults when the identical generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? By design, the experiment does not measure benefits arising from alternate generator samples or repair-enabled iterations; it measures pure detection on the same candidate to avoid confounding from generator-sampling variability.

Our empirical contribution is an artifact-grounded, fully archived confirmatory run (72 paired intents) showing a degenerate ceiling outcome (zero baseline faults) and a detailed methodological analysis explaining why that outcome follows from the preregistered contract. We conclude with precise design recommendations for future trials that can detect practical verifier utility (independent-generation arms, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model comparisons). All execution artifacts, validator traces, and analysis logs are archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.related_work:
LLM-based intent→configuration translation has been explored in emulator-based evaluations and constrained-vendor settings. Nguyen et al. present intent-based configuration generation and measured task-level accuracy in emulator settings [1]. Multi-agent and tool-augmented frameworks for intent-driven NetOps (Confucius-style systems and co-pilots) have been proposed and prototyped; these systems often integrate validators to reduce regressions but typically lack preregistered detection-evaluation against emulator-executed outcomes [2,4].

Generate–Verify–Repair and related architectures have empirical precedent in code-generation and software-repair research, where deterministic checkers and test suites validate and iteratively repair stochastic outputs; such systems motivate applying GVR to network configurations but require adaptation to network-specific semantics and runtime effects [3]. Constraint-enforcing decoding and integer-programming constrained decoding are complementary approaches that aim to reduce constraint violations at generation time; these have shown benefits in structured-output domains but direct evidence for network configuration grammars is limited in the supplied literature [5].

Classical deterministic network verification techniques (header-space analyses and policy checkers) provide precise invariants—reachability, ACL semantics, and ordering constraints—making them natural verifier candidates in NetOps GVR stacks. However, the literature lacks preregistered, paired experiments that report verifier detection rates against emulator-executed failures for identical generated candidates—an evidentiary gap our study was designed to address.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 and froze the design and analysis before observing outcomes. The primary estimand is the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The confirmatory hypothesis H1 targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 with two-sided alpha = 0.05 and power ≥ 0.80; the preregistered sample size was N = 72 pairs (≈24 pairs per topology-difficulty stratum) to allow stratified inspection.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and experimental contract. The execution_contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent, exactly one initial LLM generation was produced and that identical candidate was evaluated in two conditions. Baseline: execute the shared candidate in an isolated emulator and record emulator fault/no-fault. Guarded: run the canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on the same candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no execution); if it does not flag, execute the identical candidate and record the emulation outcome. Because only one shared candidate exists per intent, the guarded arm cannot improve outcomes by prompting or sampling alternatives—the only pathway for a paired difference is deterministic detection (verifier flags) that prevents an otherwise executed fault.

Model, adapter, and verifier configuration. The requested model recorded in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version), provider = openai_responses, max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, and temperature = null (provider default runtime sampling semantics). The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The canonical verifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0"), which implements a full_intent_constraint_validation rule set producing binary per-episode validity outcomes and structured validator_traces (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after states, violation_codes, difficulty metadata).

Task-bank construction and contamination controls. Tasks were deterministically generated using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest entry encodes: natural-language intent, a machine-structured required_sequence (ordered field changes), allowed_touched_fields, initial and expected final states, and difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard) and patterns (e.g., make_before_break, shutdown_configure_restore). The preregistration mandated exact-match contamination detection against public corpora and explicit exclusion rules; analysis/contamination_summary.csv records zero exact-match exclusions for confirmatory pairs. The confirmatory sample remained stratified as preregistered (24 pairs per stratum).

Execution protocol and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan allowed up to two additional retries for transient hosted-API errors; all retries and provider-call metadata were deterministically logged. The execution manifest records: planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 72 (one shared generation per pair). Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, cache_miss_count = 72, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 72}. The run started at 2026-08-31T06:56:23.065707Z and completed at 2026-08-31T07:06:28.665518Z (≈10.1 minutes total wall-clock execution for the complete pipeline including verification and emulation for all pairs).

Scoring and analysis procedures. The verifier outputs per-episode score and a detailed validator_trace. The primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 to construct a 2×2 paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) and an exact McNemar two-sided test when discordant pairs exist. We computed paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals for the paired difference using 10,000 resamples with bootstrap_seed = 1729 (recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Pre-specified subgroup confirmatory comparisons (topology complexity and policy type) were registered with Holm correction; given the observed ceiling outcome these subgroup tests are non-informative for confirmatory inference but remain archived for reproducibility.
sections.results:
Execution and deterministic accounting. The run completed without technical failures. Key recorded manifest values: planned_episode_count = 144; completed_episode_count = 144; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 72. Provider-call accounting matches the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics (72 completed hosted model calls, zero failed calls, zero cache hits). The artifact bundle contains 510 artifacts (artifact_hash_summary) including raw responses, validator traces, task manifests, and analysis artifacts.

Paired contingency and inferential outcomes. Aggregating across the 72 preregistered pairs produced contingency counts n_11 = 72, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (guarded × baseline). The paired estimate paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) is [0.0, 0.0], reflecting the degenerate distribution produced by the absence of discordant pairs. Per-condition summaries in analysis/condition_summary.csv record baseline success_rate = 1.0 and guarded success_rate = 1.0.

Representative validator diagnostics. Representative scoring artifacts are archived for sampled episodes (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json). Validator_trace fields across these examples indicate parsed_command_count between 2 and 6, required_command_count matching parsed counts for valid sequences, difficulty.level spanning medium/hard/very_hard, normalized_configuration matching the shared candidate, validator_version = "5.0", score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION", and violation_count = 0. These traces confirm the verifier executed on each shared candidate and produced no violation flags on the preregistered tasks.

Contamination and missingness. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports zero flagged exact-match contaminations for confirmatory pairs. analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 72 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. The absence of exclusions and technical failures simplifies interpretation but creates a ceiling effect: under shared_initial_candidate semantics, a verifier cannot reduce executed faults when baseline executions already show zero emulator-observed faults.

Sensitivity and reproducibility diagnostics. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses (treating excluded pairs as failures; bootstrap diagnostics) were executed and archived. Because no pairs were excluded and no discordant outcomes occurred, these sensitivity analyses reproduce the degenerate numeric conclusion (paired difference = 0.0). The bootstrap reproducibility is supported by analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (bootstrap_seed = 1729, bootstrap_resamples = 10000) and the full analysis artifact set archived in analysis/*.csv and analysis/*.jsonl.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory interpretation. The preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics validly measures verifier detection on identical candidates. Observing zero baseline faults yields a scientifically informative ceiling/null outcome: given the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), prompt/templates, and synthetic task bank the generator outputs were uniformly valid in the emulator; therefore the verifier had no executed failures to prevent. The numerical outputs (n_11 = 72; paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0]) are direct consequences of the preregistered contract and observed data, not an argument that verifiers are unnecessary in general.

Why the ceiling arose and what it implies. Several artifact-grounded factors contributed to the ceiling outcome: (1) deterministic task generator produced constrained, high-clarity intents with explicit required_sequence fields; (2) the generator and prompt templates (archived in execution/responses and task_manifest entries) were sufficient for gpt-5-mini to produce correct sequences for this synthetic corpus; (3) the verifier checks implemented in deterministic_netops_validator_v5 align closely with the required_sequence constraints encoded in task manifests, increasing the chance that generated outputs will satisfy both intent and verifier rules. The combined effect is an intentionally conservative confirmatory test that can validly demonstrate verifier detection when baseline errors are present but will produce a degenerate null when baseline error prevalence is negligible.

Design recommendations for measuring verifier utility. To measure practical verifier benefits, future preregistered designs should adopt one or more of the following artifact-grounded modifications (all supported by preregistration alternatives and archiveable in the same evidence framework): (A) independent-generation arms: allow separate initial generations per condition (baseline vs guarded) so verifier-triggered repairs or alternative sampling may change executed candidate distributions; (B) repair-enabled flows: permit a single deterministic repair call when the verifier flags violations and execute repaired candidates, measuring end-to-end improvement; (C) adversarial/fault-injection task banks: seed tasks with ambiguous intents, ordering subtleties, or protocol edge cases to elevate baseline error prevalence and reveal true positive/false positive tradeoffs; (D) multi-model and sampling sweeps: include multiple model versions and explicit sampling parameter settings (non-null temperatures) to quantify model- and sampling-sensitivity. Our preregistration and archived executor support all these alternative contracts and can be used for follow-on confirmatory runs without changing the core analysis machinery.

Threats to validity and caveats. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate design cleanly isolates detection but prevents verifier-mediated candidate selection from influencing the paired outcome. Construct validity: emulator-observed faults are a conservative proxy for operational harm but do not capture traffic-dependent timing or device-specific emergent failures in production. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic task bank, and one deterministic verifier; extrapolation to other models, vendor dialects, or production hardware is limited. Conclusion validity: because baseline error prevalence was zero in this corpus, the confirmatory design had no power to detect verifier benefit here. Residual risk: provenance and contamination checks found no exact-match contamination, but private training-data contamination of hosted models cannot be fully excluded and remains an acknowledged residual uncertainty.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM‑generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults and the verifier did not change outcomes (paired difference = 0.0, bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: when identical generated candidates produce no executed faults, a verifier cannot reduce executed faults under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes requires experimental contracts that permit independent or multiple generator samples, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model comparisons. The archived artifacts (responses, task manifests, verifier traces, execution manifest, and complete analysis logs) provide a reproducible baseline and a template for those follow-on confirmatory designs and power calculations (preregistration targeted N≈63 pairs for a 0.20 absolute reduction; N=72 was used to provide margin).

limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per‑condition generation, multi‑sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single‑model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling‑parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (sampling parameters unset); null indicates provider default sampling semantics determined runtime sampling behavior and is a residual uncertainty recorded in the archived configuration.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact‑match checks were applied, but private training‑data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
